Archive item 2: Research Notebook – Evaluation Methodology
Source format: Research notebook entries

Key design decisions for this round:
- Module A: Demographics (age band, housing type, employment status) – keep short, no income question (sensitive in this district).
- Module B: Service awareness (recognition of 5 named programmes, plus "other").
- Module C: Access barriers (transport, cost, waiting time, language) – use check-all-that-apply, not ranking. Ranking caused drop-off last time.
- Module D: Satisfaction (4-point, no neutral). We lost too many "don't know" responses in v2.1; better to force a lean.

Need to confirm with the grants team whether the outcome indicators must map to the new framework before we finalise the survey. I think the framework v3.2 is now the governing document for all outcome reporting, but I should check the latest memo.

---

**3 May 2024 (Fri), 14:15 – Field prep**

Met with the two field coordinators for the Tampines and Jurong sites. Both confirmed that the April pilot had a 62% response rate, which is acceptable but not great. Main reasons for non-response: "too long" (n=??, maybe 18) and "not interested" (n=??, maybe 12). We will shorten the intro script and add a QR code for online completion as a backup.

Also discussed the translation protocol. The questionnaire must be available in English, Chinese (Simplified? – the community uses Simplified for written materials), and Malay. We do not have Tamil yet; need to source a certified translator. The previous translator (for v2.1) was slow and we had to chase. Suggest we ask the grants team for a recommended vendor.

Field schedule for May:
- 13 May: Tampines site – training session for enumerators (10:00–12:00).
- 15 May: Jurong site – training session (14:00–16:00).
- 20–31 May: Data collection window. Aim for n=300 per site, but realistically n=250.

---

**6 May 2024 (Mon), 10:05 – Framework check**

I found the governance memo from the RRI Research Committee dated 12 March 2024. It states that **Outcome Evaluation Framework v3.2's version is 3.2. Record status: current.** and that this version is the current controlled version for all new studies starting after 1 April 2024. The memo also says that v3.1 is archived and should not be used for new data collection, though existing longitudinal studies may continue under v3.1 until their next reporting cycle.

Key changes in v3.2 (from the summary in the memo):
- Indicator definitions for "service completion" and "client satisfaction" have been tightened.
- Added a new indicator: "referral uptake within 30 days".
- The reporting table format has changed – row headers are now standardised across all RRI units.

Since our pilot is a new study, we must use v3.2. I will update the survey cover page and the data dictionary accordingly. The old v3.1 indicator codes (e.g., "SAT-01", "ACC-02") are no longer valid for new submissions.

---

**8 May 2024 (Wed), 16:20 – Survey draft v0.4**

Circulated draft v0.4 to the field coordinators and the grants manager for review. Changes from v0.3:
- Removed the "household income" question (as planned).
- Added a "referral source" question (how did you hear about this programme?) – this maps to the new referral uptake indicator in v3.2.
- Shortened the open-ended question at the end to a single line, not a box.

One concern from the grants manager: the survey does not yet include a question on "programme awareness" that matches the v3.2 indicator definition. The framework defines awareness as "proportion of target population who can name at least two services offered by the programme". Our current question (Module B) only asks for recognition, not unaided recall. I will revise Module B to include one open-ended recall question first, then the recognition list.

---

**10 May 2024 (Fri), 09:15 – Instrument run summary (training session prep)**
**11 May 2024 (Sat), 14:40 – Field note: Orchard Road pilot site**

Met with the site coordinator at the drop-in centre. The room we planned for the survey corner is being used for a storage overflow until the end of the month. We have a smaller table near the entrance, but it is next to the queue for the information counter. I think the noise will be manageable, but we may need to shift the referral source question to the end so respondents are not rushed while the queue builds.

Also noted that the centre's wifi drops intermittently in the afternoon. The tablet-based survey will need an offline mode. I will check with IT whether the v3.2 form is already configured for offline capture. If not, we may need to fall back to paper for the first two weeks. The data entry burden will be higher, but it is better than losing responses.

---

**14 May 2024 (Tue), 09:05 – Instrument run summary (pilot dry run #1)**

Dry run completed at the office with three volunteer staff acting as respondents. Total time per survey: 7–9 minutes. No major skips or errors. Two observations:

- The open-ended recall question (Module B, q1) was answered with a single word by two of the three volunteers ("transport", "food"). The question wording says "name at least two services" – we may need a probe prompt on the tablet, e.g., "Anything else?" to encourage a fuller response.
- The referral source question (Module C, q3) worked fine, but one volunteer asked whether "referred by a friend" and "referred by family" should be separate codes. I think we can keep them combined for now; the framework only asks for the source category, not the relationship detail.

No other issues. The survey cover page shows the v3.2 version number correctly, and the data dictionary has been updated with the new indicator codes. I will ask the grants manager to confirm the cover page wording before we print.

---

**16 May 2024 (Thu), 11:20 – Notebook entry: sampling plan adjustment**

The original sampling plan called for recruiting at the drop-in centre only. After reviewing the v3.2 indicator definitions, I realised the "referral uptake within 30 days" indicator requires us to track whether a referred client actually attends a service within 30 days. We cannot measure this if we only recruit at the centre, because we would not see clients who were referred but never showed up.

I have added a secondary recruitment point: the two community kitchens in the same district. This will give us a small cohort of clients who were referred but may not have attended the centre. The field coordinators have agreed, and the grant budget has a small line item for transport tokens for the kitchen sites. I will draft a short addendum to the sampling plan and send it to the Research Committee for approval. The addendum does not change the survey instrument, only the recruitment locations.

---

**20 May 2024 (Mon), 15:50 – Field observation: Toa Payoh kitchen site**

Visited one of the community kitchens to check the space. The kitchen manager is supportive and has set aside a corner table for us. The kitchen is busiest between 11:00 and 13:00, so we will schedule recruitment from 14:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. One concern: the kitchen does not have a private room, and the survey will be conducted in the open dining area. Some clients may be reluctant to answer the "referral source" question if others can overhear. I will include a note in the field protocol that the interviewer should offer the option to complete the survey at the counter if the respondent prefers more privacy.

documents.title: Research Notebook – Evaluation Methodology
documents.content:
Key design decisions for this round:
- Module A: Demographics (age band, housing type, employment status) – keep short, no income question (sensitive in this district).
- Module B: Service awareness (recognition of 5 named programmes, plus "other").
- Module C: Access barriers (transport, cost, waiting time, language) – use check-all-that-apply, not ranking. Ranking caused drop-off last time.
- Module D: Satisfaction (4-point, no neutral). We lost too many "don't know" responses in v2.1; better to force a lean.

Need to confirm with the grants team whether the outcome indicators must map to the new framework before we finalise the survey. I think the framework v3.2 is now the governing document for all outcome reporting, but I should check the latest memo.

---

**3 May 2024 (Fri), 14:15 – Field prep**

Met with the two field coordinators for the Tampines and Jurong sites. Both confirmed that the April pilot had a 62% response rate, which is acceptable but not great. Main reasons for non-response: "too long" (n=??, maybe 18) and "not interested" (n=??, maybe 12). We will shorten the intro script and add a QR code for online completion as a backup.

Also discussed the translation protocol. The questionnaire must be available in English, Chinese (Simplified? – the community uses Simplified for written materials), and Malay. We do not have Tamil yet; need to source a certified translator. The previous translator (for v2.1) was slow and we had to chase. Suggest we ask the grants team for a recommended vendor.

Field schedule for May:
- 13 May: Tampines site – training session for enumerators (10:00–12:00).
- 15 May: Jurong site – training session (14:00–16:00).
- 20–31 May: Data collection window. Aim for n=300 per site, but realistically n=250.

---

**6 May 2024 (Mon), 10:05 – Framework check**

I found the governance memo from the RRI Research Committee dated 12 March 2024. It states that **Outcome Evaluation Framework v3.2's version is 3.2. Record status: current.** and that this version is the current controlled version for all new studies starting after 1 April 2024. The memo also says that v3.1 is archived and should not be used for new data collection, though existing longitudinal studies may continue under v3.1 until their next reporting cycle.

Key changes in v3.2 (from the summary in the memo):
- Indicator definitions for "service completion" and "client satisfaction" have been tightened.
- Added a new indicator: "referral uptake within 30 days".
- The reporting table format has changed – row headers are now standardised across all RRI units.

Since our pilot is a new study, we must use v3.2. I will update the survey cover page and the data dictionary accordingly. The old v3.1 indicator codes (e.g., "SAT-01", "ACC-02") are no longer valid for new submissions.

---

**8 May 2024 (Wed), 16:20 – Survey draft v0.4**

Circulated draft v0.4 to the field coordinators and the grants manager for review. Changes from v0.3:
- Removed the "household income" question (as planned).
- Added a "referral source" question (how did you hear about this programme?) – this maps to the new referral uptake indicator in v3.2.
- Shortened the open-ended question at the end to a single line, not a box.

One concern from the grants manager: the survey does not yet include a question on "programme awareness" that matches the v3.2 indicator definition. The framework defines awareness as "proportion of target population who can name at least two services offered by the programme". Our current question (Module B) only asks for recognition, not unaided recall. I will revise Module B to include one open-ended recall question first, then the recognition list.

---

**10 May 2024 (Fri), 09:15 – Instrument run summary (training session prep)**

documents.title: Research Notebook – Evaluation Methodology
documents.content:
**11 May 2024 (Sat), 14:40 – Field note: Orchard Road pilot site**

Met with the site coordinator at the drop-in centre. The room we planned for the survey corner is being used for a storage overflow until the end of the month. We have a smaller table near the entrance, but it is next to the queue for the information counter. I think the noise will be manageable, but we may need to shift the referral source question to the end so respondents are not rushed while the queue builds.

Also noted that the centre's wifi drops intermittently in the afternoon. The tablet-based survey will need an offline mode. I will check with IT whether the v3.2 form is already configured for offline capture. If not, we may need to fall back to paper for the first two weeks. The data entry burden will be higher, but it is better than losing responses.

---

**14 May 2024 (Tue), 09:05 – Instrument run summary (pilot dry run #1)**

Dry run completed at the office with three volunteer staff acting as respondents. Total time per survey: 7–9 minutes. No major skips or errors. Two observations:

- The open-ended recall question (Module B, q1) was answered with a single word by two of the three volunteers ("transport", "food"). The question wording says "name at least two services" – we may need a probe prompt on the tablet, e.g., "Anything else?" to encourage a fuller response.
- The referral source question (Module C, q3) worked fine, but one volunteer asked whether "referred by a friend" and "referred by family" should be separate codes. I think we can keep them combined for now; the framework only asks for the source category, not the relationship detail.

No other issues. The survey cover page shows the v3.2 version number correctly, and the data dictionary has been updated with the new indicator codes. I will ask the grants manager to confirm the cover page wording before we print.

---

**16 May 2024 (Thu), 11:20 – Notebook entry: sampling plan adjustment**

The original sampling plan called for recruiting at the drop-in centre only. After reviewing the v3.2 indicator definitions, I realised the "referral uptake within 30 days" indicator requires us to track whether a referred client actually attends a service within 30 days. We cannot measure this if we only recruit at the centre, because we would not see clients who were referred but never showed up.

I have added a secondary recruitment point: the two community kitchens in the same district. This will give us a small cohort of clients who were referred but may not have attended the centre. The field coordinators have agreed, and the grant budget has a small line item for transport tokens for the kitchen sites. I will draft a short addendum to the sampling plan and send it to the Research Committee for approval. The addendum does not change the survey instrument, only the recruitment locations.

---

**20 May 2024 (Mon), 15:50 – Field observation: Toa Payoh kitchen site**

Visited one of the community kitchens to check the space. The kitchen manager is supportive and has set aside a corner table for us. The kitchen is busiest between 11:00 and 13:00, so we will schedule recruitment from 14:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. One concern: the kitchen does not have a private room, and the survey will be conducted in the open dining area. Some clients may be reluctant to answer the "referral source" question if others can overhear. I will include a note in the field protocol that the interviewer should offer the option to complete the survey at the counter if the respondent prefers more privacy.
